enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
555 AM MDT Thu Oct 22 2026

...New AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 537 AM MDT Thu Oct 22 2026

 - Warm temperatures over the next couple days, with lowland highs
   in the 80s. This is slightly above normal for late October.

 - Widespread chances for showers and thunderstorms return Thursday
   night through Friday as moisture moves north into the region. 
   Some stronger storms could result in flash flooding, damaging 
   winds, and large hail.

 - The flood threat lingers for eastern areas this weekend before storm
   chances decrease early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1028 PM MDT Wed Oct 21 2026

A very active weather pattern will bring a widespread chance of 
strong thunderstorms and heavy rain to Southern New Mexico and Far
West Texas Thursday through Saturday. A deep moist southerly flow
continues between a strong ridge of high pressure over central 
Texas and a deep low pressure system centered along the California
coast. As the low pressure system begins to move inland. 
Scattered to numerous showers will occur over Arizona and western 
portions of New Mexico northward into the Great Basin and parts of
Colorado. Favorable forcing and lift will interact with the moist
unstable air mass to generate widespread thunderstorms across the
local area in the afternoon and evening. The highest amount of 
activity will be concentrated in the Gila region and nearby areas 
mostly west of Rio Grande extending to the Arizona Border. 

There is a a marginal risk of severe thunderstorms for areas west
of the Rio Grande on Thursday with possible large hail, strong
wind gusts, and maybe a low probability short lived weak tornado.
Widespread thunderstorms will also produce periods of heavy rain
with a potential for flash flooding, especially in the Gila Region
and nearby surrounding areas. A flash flood watch is in effect for
that area from noon Thursday through 6am Friday morning. Potential
rain amounts are between 1 and 2 inches with isolated higher 
amounts in the Gila Region.   

The active weather pattern will continue on Friday widespread
showers and thunderstorms over portions of south central  New 
Mexico centered on the Rio Grande valley from El Paso north to 
Albuquerque. There will be a marginal risk of severe thunderstorms
Friday afternoon and evening. There will also be a chance of 
excessive rainfall with a potential for flooding. 

A similar situation will develop on Saturday with additional
excessive rainfall with a potential for flooding for areas
generally east of the Rio Grande. Strong thunderstorms with large
hail and strong winds will be also be possible. 

The low pressure system and the moisture will lift out of the
local area Sunday in to Monday with a return drier and calmer
weather conditions for a few days. Long term outlook does have a
chance of showers returning late next week. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 537 AM MDT Thu Oct 22 2026

Shower and storm chances increase through the day and this
evening. Isolated showers develop during the day, but confidence
is low in timing and placement. Higher confidence in direct 
impacts for KTCS and KDMN later today from TS with gusts to 40kts
possible at KDMN. Low chance of CIGs falling to MVFR levels.
Convection lifts north overnight. Light winds this morning, then
gusting to 20kts from S-SE this afternoon. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 537 AM MDT Thu Oct 22 2026

No fire weather concerns are forecast through the weekend. Storm 
chances increase out west this afternoon and evening, pushing NE
and exiting the area overnight. Large hail and damaging winds are
possible west of the RGV through the evening. Heavy rainfall is
possible in the Gila through tonight with isolated amounts of 
2-3". Lower chance of storms further east in the short-term. Winds
today will be modestly breezy from the S-SE. Temperatures today
will be seasonably warm with better mixing than yesterday, but not
great. High storm chances push east Fri/Sat along with the flash 
flood and severe threat. Winds stay modestly breezy into the 
weekend, favoring a S-SE direction. Temps cool to near and below 
normal over the weekend.

Min RHs range from 50-75% in the Gila today, 25-50% elsewhere;
then 30-50% lowlands and 45-75% mtns through Sat. Vent rates will
be fair to very good.

&&
